rules.statement: Don't ask a docs site to add its own build script that checks each `var(--nc-…)` read is defined in the brand tokens when the pinned NCodeGroup/docs toolchain already fails the site build on undefined or private token reads.
rules.why: The pinned toolchain (ADR-1012, `src/brand/tokens.mjs`) already reports every undefined `--nc-` read and every private-primitive read on each pull request, so a second check would only repeat it.
rules.check: Before reporting a missing token-definition check, look at the NCodeGroup/docs version the docs workflow pins and whether its build validates `--nc-` reads; report only if the pinned version predates that check.

rules.statement: Don't ask docs site components to replace font-size, font-weight or line-height literals with the brand's `--nc-text-*`, `--nc-weight-*` or `--nc-leading-*` tokens, or to switch to a type role's `font` shorthand just to remove the literals.
rules.why: Those tokens are private brand primitives that any release may change and the toolchain build fails a component that reads them; no public token holds those single values, so the literals are the component's own design values, and switching to a type role's shorthand changes the component's look.
rules.check: Before reporting repeated type-scale literals, check whether a public (non-primitive) brand token holds exactly that value; if only private primitives do, don't report.

rules.statement: End a .NET regex meant to match a whole string with `\z`, not `$`.
rules.why: In .NET `$` also matches just before a trailing newline, so a value with a trailing newline would wrongly count as a full match.
rules.check: Look for regex patterns built or written as `^...$` that are used for whole-string matching (globs, identifiers, validation) and check they use `\z` instead.

rules.statement: When code translates glob patterns to regular expressions, give each translation branch its own test: `?`, `*`, `**`, `**/`, escaped regex metacharacters such as `.`, and any case normalisation of the input.
rules.why: A regression in an untested branch leaves the suite green while the matcher selects different items from the ones the consumer expects.
rules.check: For a change to a glob-to-regex converter or its tests, check that each token kind it handles and each input normalisation has a positive and a negative test case.
